text:
Anna: Heads up — after the int4 calibration rollout on dedicated-3 we see a 12% tail latency regression at p99 for generation requests. Not huge but consistent across shards. :eyes:
Raj: Can you paste the per-token breakdown? Is it a kernel switch or batching change?
Anna: Pasted below from a sampling of traced requests (canary window). Note kernel counters and KV hit rates are included.
Anna: ```
sample_id: c7a2
seq_len: 128
per_token_ms: [first_token: 12, avg: 3.2, p95: 7.8, p99: 24.6]
kernel_counters: {int4_kernels: 62, int8_kernels: 18, fp8_kernels: 20}
kv_cache: {hits: 68%, misses: 32%}
batch_sizes: mode=4, bimodal tail at 16
calib_profile: mixprec_v2_alpha
```
Maria: Interesting — kernel_counters show a lot of int4 but still a non-trivial fp8 fallback. Could the calibration be increasing kernel fallbacks for longer sequences?
Simon: Also check batching heuristics: the new batch timeout tweak (batch_timeout_ms=6 -> 4) went out in the same deploy. Shorter timeout could shift many requests into smaller batches which hurts int4 throughput on our tensor cores.
Raj: Good catch. If small batches + int4 lead to more kernel switches (int4->fp8), overhead per token goes up. Need kernel switch counters across step boundaries.
Anna: perf-bot trace attached below (snip):
perf-bot: ```
TRACE START sample c7a2
step 0: select_kernel=int4 (setup_ms: 0.9)
step 1: execute_int4 (exec_ms: 1.9)
step 2: select_kernel=fp8 (switch_ms: 6.8)
step 2: execute_fp8 (exec_ms: 9.1)
KV_CACHE_LOOKUP: miss
TRACE END
```
Maria: Those switch_ms numbers are the smoking gun. Kernel selection moving mid-sequence is expensive. Do we have a knob to prefer a stable kernel for full request once chosen?
Raj: We do: `kernel_policy: prefer_stable` but it wasn't enabled for mixprec_v2_alpha. We can flip it in routing for the canary pool. That will avoid switching even if small kernel wins on single step.
Simon: Before flipping, can we repro locally with a toy workload that mirrors the bimodal batch distribution? I can push a job that replays a minute of traffic with exact seq/batch mix.
Anna: Yes please. Also I want to compare per-token cost with/without KV cache hits. When misses happen we see longer sequences and more fallback.
Maria: FYI I plotted kv_hit vs p99 for the samples — when hit < 75% p99 jumps ~9-13ms consistently. Looks like cache pressure region.
Raj: Action plan: 1) Simon runs local replay, measures kernel switch counters and per-token latency with current batch_timeout. 2) Flip `kernel_policy: prefer_stable` in canary routing for mixprec_v2_alpha to see regression revert. 3) Roll back batch_timeout tweak if replay shows small batches amplify switch cost. 4) Investigate KV cache admission thresholds to improve hit% for common prefixes.
Anna: I'll open a short-lived canary and tag the affected dedicated-3 instances. If we flip the policy we should be able to see effect within 10 min.
Simon: Starting replay job now. ETA 12m. Posting results to this thread.
perf-bot: replay_job_321 started by Simon at 1965432205
Simon: Replay done. Quick numbers: baseline (policy=balanced, batch_timeout=6): p99=142ms. current (policy=balanced, timeout=4): p99=160ms. policy=prefer_stable, timeout=4: p99=138ms. Kernel-switches per request: baseline=0.12, current=0.43, stable=0.08. KV hit% unchanged in replay (70%).
Anna: Great — flipping policy looks promising. Can we do a targeted route change for the canary only?
Raj: Yes, creating a route override: `route: mixprec-v2-alpha -> policy=prefer_stable` for tag dedicated-3-canary. I'll push now.
perf-bot: route_override_applied for dedicated-3-canary at 1965432450
Anna: Monitoring dashboards... p95 unchanged, p99 dropped back to ~139ms on canary. :thumbsup:
Maria: Still want to tune KV cache to avoid the 68-72% hit region. Suggest increasing prefix retention for repeated short prompts; might trade memory but lowers misses.
Simon: Also propose a batching heuristic change: make batch_timeout adaptive based on recent batch size variance. If bimodal tail detected, increase timeout to preferentially combine small requests for a short period.
Raj: Agree — I'll open a PR with adaptive timeout + metric guards. For immediate relief we keep prefer_stable on the canary while we iterate.
Anna: Good. I'll leave canary running for an hour then decide. Thanks all.
Simon: Noted — will include kernel switch counters in the rollout dashboard so we catch regressions early.
Maria: Also adding an alert: kernel-switch-rate > 0.25 for 5m triggers auto-revert.
Anna: Perfect. Closing loop once we confirm KV changes. :white_check_mark:
